sections.instructions: Watch the documentary Reel Injun, by Catherine Bainbridge, Neil Diamond and Jeremiah Hayes. Questions taken from NFB.com. In these questions and main point summaries, the terms Indian, First Nations, Aboriginals, Indigenous Peoples, Natives, Native American and politically incorrect “Injun” are used in reference to the filmmakers' choice and style of script writing. /30

prompts.label: What are the consequences of distorted representations of Indigenous people with regard to their identity, self-esteem and social and cultural development?
Why would western culture treat Indians as myths or dinosaurs?
The silent era portrayed Native people as noble; how did that come to be?
Do you think that the kids in the summer camp sequence in Reel Injun were only encountered Native people in Hollywood movies?
According to Hollywood's criteria, what does it take to be a good or noble Indian?
By developing the Tonto speech, did Hollywood harm the existing Native languages spoken by US tribes?
What are some of the misguided notions surrounding the Indian princess Pocahontas?
When John Wayne shoots a dead Indian that was dug up from a burial ground in the eyes to make sure he will not be going to the spirit world, what kind of message is Hollywood sending?
What about the use of Native languages in the movies: Is it desirable in order to improve the pride and self-esteem of First Nations people?

Retrace the history and the meaning of this famously racist pronouncement by General Philip Sheridan: “A Good Injun . . . is a Dead Injun.” Why would Hollywood use such neo-colonialist propaganda to confuse the feelings of young Native people?
Regarding the notion of human beings, why does John Trudell place so much emphasis on language as an instrument of war?

In the 1970s, the US government infiltrated a tribal council (on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation in the town of Wounded Knee) and in 1973 AIM activists seized the town. Retrace the framework of events that led to the uprising.
Director Neil Diamond mentioned that he found the answers he was looking for in the North. What exactly was the object of his quest?
On what basis can we say that Atanarjuat is the “most Native” movie ever made?

sections.instructions: Please visit the following document to learn about the issues in Attawapiskat. Read through the document, and use the additional links on the document as you see fit to learn more about the issue. This document was made in 2011. The community has changed since then. Therefore, part of your task is to also conduct additional research to learn more about Attawapiskat today. As part of your assignment, you must provide links to at least three sources (news articles, videos, reports, photos, etc) that are dated from 2023 onwards. Attawapiskat is now seen as a community in crisis that is living in poor conditions. Explain this description using information from the document. Your report must include the following elements: current data dated at least 2015 and above; information regarding the suicide, housing, health care, etc. crisis; what could the future hold?; what could help this community?; 3 current sources from 2023 or later. Respond in any form you would like: paragraph form, letter, presentation, video, visual display. /16

prompts.label: Community report: explain why Attawapiskat is seen as a community in crisis living in poor conditions, using the 2011 document plus your own research (current data from 2015 onwards, suicide/housing/health care crisis, what the future could hold, what could help, and 3 current sources from 2023 or later).
